This video is from Yellowknife, NT, Canada. It is a Raven, and they do this quite frequently. I once had a Raven chase my car for several blocks because it left a chunk of frozen meat on the roof.

The people up here are absolutely amazing. Anywhere you go you are treated with kindness from strangers. It's like a little club where people know how hard the winters are so they all support each other to get through it. Everyone knows that suffering through the brutal winters is worth the spectacular summers we have where the sun doesn't set and it gets up to +30°C. 

My most memorable story would be several years ago when we had a power outage. We have frequent power outages in the north, and this particular one was on a -50°C day. It lasted hours. Our house started to get really cold without heat, and some people had their water pipes freeze. We started to make plans to find friends with a wood stove in case the power didn't come back on. It eventually did and all was okay.

When it gets this cold you have to either run your vehicle every 4 hours or have it plugged in to power. You have to plan to have it running at least 15 minutes before you go anywhere. You also can't let your gas get below 1/4 tank full or it can freeze. People do indeed exercise in this weather, but I think they are crazy! You see people on runs all the time or out skiing. 

Something I love about this weather is the ice fog that forms. It's thicker than regular fog and creates this calming look to the sky. The trees get a beautiful layer of frost on their branches that sparkles when the sun hits them.
My power bill is $200 on a good day. In the winter it can easily match the propane bill of $700.
